lessons.title: From One Welder to a Workshop
lessons.body:
Moving from a one-man operation to a workshop means you stop being the only person who welds and start being the person who runs the business. In most African cities, the first step is to rent a small spaceâoften a 20ft by 30ft room or a covered yard in an industrial area. Expect to pay between $150 and $400 per month depending on location and whether you have three-phase power. You need at least one 3-phase 415V supply for a 250-amp AC/DC TIG welder and a plasma cutter. If three-phase is not available, a 7.5kVA generator will run a 200-amp inverter welder but will cost about $0.30 per hour in fuel.

Your first hire should be an apprentice, not a qualified welder. An apprentice costs $80â$150 per month and can cut, grind, and hold pieces while you weld. This frees you to take on two jobs at once. As you win more work, add a second welder. Pay a skilled aluminium TIG welder $300â$500 per month in most African markets. Keep your own hands on the torch for complex jobs, but let your team handle simple frames and repairs.

Organise your workshop into three zones: a cutting and grinding bay, a welding bay with good ventilation, and a finishing and assembly area. Buy or build steel tables at 900mm height. Use firebricks to line your welding table. Keep a 5kg CO2 fire extinguisher within reach. Label everythingâargon cylinders, filler rods (4043 and 5356), and consumables. A clean shop reduces mistakes and impresses clients who visit.

Track your jobs on a whiteboard or notebook. Write down the client name, job description, agreed price, and deadline. At the end of each week, calculate your revenue, material costs, and labour costs. If your profit is less than 30% of revenue, raise your prices or cut waste. A workshop that does not track numbers will grow broke even as it grows busy.

lessons.title: Buying Equipment as You Grow
lessons.body:
Do not buy everything at once. Buy equipment when a specific job or a steady stream of work justifies it. Start with a 200-amp AC/DC TIG welder with a foot pedal and a #17 torch. A good used machine from brands like Miller, Lincoln, or ESAB costs $800â$1,500. A new Chinese equivalent (e.g., Everlast or Jasic) costs $500â$900 and works fine for most aluminium jobs up to 6mm thick. You also need a plasma cutter for clean cutsâa 40-amp unit costs $400â$700 and will cut up to 10mm aluminium.

As your workload grows, add a second TIG welder so two people can work at once. Then buy a MIG welder with a spool gun for thicker aluminium (above 6mm). A 250-amp MIG with spool gun costs $1,200â$2,000. This machine pays for itself on jobs like truck beds, boat hulls, and large gates. Next, invest in a 3-ton hydraulic press brake and a sheet metal shear. These let you bend and cut your own aluminium sheets, saving you 20â30% on material costs. A used press brake costs $2,000â$4,000; a shear costs $1,500â$3,000.

Buy argon cylinders outright instead of renting. A 50-litre cylinder costs $200â$300, and refills cost $40â$60. You need at least two cylinders so you never run out mid-job. Buy filler rods in bulkâ10kg boxes of 4043 (for general work) and 5356 (for stronger, marine-grade joints). A 10kg box costs $80â$120. Keep a stock of tungsten electrodes (2% lanthanated, 1.6mm and 2.4mm), ceramic cups, collets, and gas lenses. These consumables are cheap but running out stops work.

Maintain your equipment. Blow out dust from welder internals every month. Check torch cables for cracks. Replace worn contact tips on the MIG. A well-maintained machine lasts 10 years; a neglected one lasts two. Keep a simple logbook for each machine: date of purchase, service dates, and repairs. When you need a loan or grant, this logbook proves you are serious.

lessons.title: Training and Hiring
lessons.body:
Hiring the right person is harder than welding. Do not hire based on a certificate alone. Test every candidate with a practical job: give them two pieces of 3mm aluminium, a TIG welder, and 30 minutes. Ask them to make a butt weld and a T-joint. Then cut the weld in half and inspect for penetration, porosity, and cracks. A good welder produces a clean, consistent bead with no holes. A bad welder makes a pretty bead that breaks under load. Pay for the testâ$10â$20 is fair.

When you hire, start with a one-month trial. Pay a fair daily rate: $10â$20 per day for a skilled welder, $5â$8 for a helper. After one month, if they show up on time, follow safety rules, and produce good work, offer a monthly salary. Add a bonus for jobs completed ahead of schedule or under material budget. This motivates without raising fixed costs.

Train your team every week. Spend one hour on Friday afternoon on a specific skill: how to set the AC balance for clean aluminium, how to avoid burn-through on thin sheet, how to tack without distortion. Use scrap metal for practice. Show them a good weld and a bad weld side by side. Explain why one fails. Let them practice while you watch and correct. This weekly training costs you one hour of production but doubles your teamâs value in six months.

Document your own methods. Write down your settings for common jobs: 3mm aluminium sheet, 1.6mm tungsten, 70% AC balance, 120 amps, 15 CFH argon. Write down your jig designs and clamping tricks. Put this in a notebook or a WhatsApp group for your team. When you hire a new person, they learn from your notes, not from trial and error. This saves time and reduces costly mistakes. A team that learns together stays together and makes you money.

lessons.title: Certification and Quality Standards
lessons.body:
Certification opens doors to bigger contracts. In most African countries, the national standards bodyâsuch as KEBS in Kenya, SON in Nigeria, or SABS in South Africaâoffers welding certification. The common international standard is ISO 9606 for welder qualification. To get certified, you need to pass a test on specific joints and positions. For aluminium, you will likely test on 3mm and 6mm plate, butt and T-joints, in flat and horizontal positions. The test costs $100â$300 and takes one day. Prepare by practicing the exact test pieces for two weeks.

Once you are certified, your business can bid on government and NGO contracts that require proof of quality. You can also certify your workshop to ISO 9001, but that is expensive and not necessary at first. Instead, create your own quality control (QC) system. For every job, record the welderâs name, the machine settings, the filler rod used, and the date. Take photos of critical welds. If a client complains, you can trace the problem. This simple system shows professionalism and wins repeat business.

Quality also means using the right materials. Never substitute 4043 filler for 5356 on a marine jobâ5356 is stronger and more corrosion-resistant. Never weld dirty aluminium; clean it with a stainless steel brush dedicated to aluminium only. Use acetone or methylated spirits to remove oil and grease. Keep your tungsten sharp and your gas flow correct (10â15 CFH for most jobs). A clean, consistent weld is your best advertisement.

Offer a warranty on your work. For structural jobs, offer a one-year warranty against defective welds. For decorative jobs, offer six months. Put it in writing. This builds trust and justifies a higher price. If a weld fails, fix it for free and learn why it failed. Your reputation is worth more than any single job. Word of mouth in African business communities travels fastâboth good and bad.

lessons.title: Finding Larger Contracts
lessons.body:
Larger contracts come from three places: construction companies, manufacturing firms, and government tenders. Start with construction. Visit building sites and ask for the site manager. Show them photos of your workâaluminium windows, doors, railings, and roofing. Offer a free sample: make a small window frame and give it to them. If they like it, they will call you for the next project. A single apartment block can need 50â100 aluminium windows, worth $5,000â$15,000 in fabrication and installation.

Manufacturing firms need aluminium jigs, machine guards, trolleys, and workbenches. Visit factories that make food products, cosmetics, or furniture. Ask to speak to the maintenance manager. Offer to make a prototype of a jig they need. Charge for materials but not labour for the first one. If it works, you become their go-to welder. These contracts are repeat businessâmonthly orders of $500â$2,000.

Government tenders are published on national procurement websites and in newspapers. You need a registered business, a tax compliance certificate, and often a certification. Start with small tendersâschool desks, hospital beds, or fencing for a local clinic. Bid competitively but do not underprice. Include your material costs, labour, transport, and a 20% profit margin. Attend the tender opening to learn how others bid. After a few losses, you will know the right price.

To win larger contracts, you must be reliable. Deliver on time. If you promise a job in two weeks, finish in 12 days. Communicate daily with the client. Send photos of progress. When you finish, clean the site and remove all scrap. A happy client gives you a reference letter. Use that letter in your next bid. Keep a folder of reference letters, photos, and certificates. This is your portfolio. In Africa, relationships matter as much as price. Be honest, be on time, and be easy to work with.

lessons.title: A 12-Month Growth Plan
lessons.body:
Month 1â3: Stabilise your one-man operation. Track every job and cost. Save 20% of profit. Buy a second argon cylinder and a stock of 4043 and 5356 filler rods. Practice TIG on 3mm and 6mm aluminium until you can weld clean beads in flat and horizontal positions. Write down your settings. Open a separate bank account for the business. Register your business name with the local authority.

Month 4â6: Hire your first apprentice. Train them on cutting, grinding, and clamping. Buy a plasma cutter. Start offering a one-year warranty on structural work. Visit 10 construction sites and 5 factories. Give out 20 business cards and a simple flyer with photos of your work. Aim for your first contract over $1,000. Save 30% of profit for equipment.

Month 7â9: Hire a skilled welder. Buy a MIG welder with spool gun if you are doing jobs above 6mm. Get certified to ISO 9606 or the national equivalent. Create a QC logbook. Start bidding on small government tenders. Increase your prices by 10% if you are fully booked. Move to a larger workshop if you have outgrown your space. Aim for monthly revenue of $3,000â$5,000.

Month 10â12: Buy a press brake and shear if you are bending and cutting your own sheets. Hire a second welder or a dedicated finisher. Apply for a business loan or grant using your logbooks and reference letters. Target one large contract worth $10,000 or more. Offer training to other welders for a feeâ$50 per day per student. By month 12, your goal is to have a team of 3â5 people, a certified workshop, and a waiting list of clients. Review your year: what worked, what did not, and what you will change. Then write your next 12-month plan. Growth is a habit, not an event.

quiz.q: What is the first step to move from a one-man operation to a workshop?
options: B) Rent a small space with three-phase power
quiz.explanation: Renting a small space with three-phase power is the foundational step for a workshop.

quiz.q: How much should you expect to pay for an apprentice per month in most African markets?
quiz.explanation: Apprentices typically cost $80â$150 per month.

quiz.q: What is the recommended height for a welding table?
quiz.explanation: A 900mm height is ergonomic for most welders.

quiz.q: What should you do if your weekly profit is less than 30% of revenue?
options: B) Raise prices or cut waste
quiz.explanation: A profit margin below 30% signals a need to raise prices or reduce costs.

quiz.q: Which TIG welder should you start with for aluminium?
quiz.explanation: Aluminium TIG welding requires AC/DC capability, and 200 amps is sufficient for most jobs.

quiz.q: What is the typical cost of a 40-amp plasma cutter?
quiz.explanation: A 40-amp plasma cutter costs around $400â$700.

quiz.q: Why should you buy argon cylinders instead of renting?
options: B) They are cheaper in the long run
D) They are easier to refill
quiz.explanation: Buying cylinders saves money over time compared to rental fees.

quiz.q: Which filler rod is best for marine-grade aluminium?
quiz.explanation: 5356 filler is stronger and more corrosion-resistant for marine applications.

quiz.q: How often should you blow out dust from welder internals?
quiz.explanation: Monthly cleaning prevents dust buildup and overheating.

quiz.q: What is the best way to test a welder before hiring?
options: C) Give a practical welding test
quiz.explanation: A practical test reveals actual skill better than certificates or interviews.

quiz.q: What is a fair daily rate for a skilled welder in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Skilled welders typically earn $10â$20 per day.

quiz.q: How often should you train your team?
quiz.explanation: Weekly one-hour training sessions improve skills consistently.

quiz.q: What should you document for common jobs?
quiz.explanation: Recording settings and methods helps standardise quality and train new hires.

quiz.q: Which standard is commonly used for welder qualification?
quiz.explanation: ISO 9606 is the international standard for welder qualification.

quiz.q: What is the approximate cost of a welder certification test?
quiz.explanation: Certification tests typically cost $100â$300.

quiz.q: Why should you never substitute 4043 filler for 5356 on a marine job?
options: B) 5356 is stronger and more corrosion-resistant
C) 4043 melts at a lower temperature
quiz.explanation: 5356 provides better strength and corrosion resistance for marine environments.

quiz.q: What is the recommended gas flow for most TIG jobs?
quiz.explanation: 10â15 CFH is the typical argon flow rate for TIG welding.

quiz.q: What type of warranty should you offer on structural jobs?
quiz.explanation: A one-year warranty on structural work builds trust and justifies higher prices.

quiz.q: Where can you find government tenders?
quiz.explanation: Government tenders are published on official procurement websites and newspapers.

quiz.q: What should you include in a tender bid?
options: B) Material, labour, transport, and 20% profit
C) A fixed price without breakdown
quiz.explanation: A comprehensive bid covers all costs plus a reasonable profit margin.

quiz.q: What is a good way to build trust with a construction client?
quiz.explanation: A free sample demonstrates your quality and commitment.

quiz.q: What should you do after finishing a large contract?
options: B) Ask for a reference letter
quiz.explanation: A reference letter serves as proof of quality for future bids.

quiz.q: In the 12-month plan, what should you do in months 1â3?
options: C) Track every job and save 20% of profit
quiz.explanation: The first three months focus on stabilising operations and saving.

quiz.q: When should you hire your first apprentice?
quiz.explanation: Hiring an apprentice is recommended in months 4â6.

quiz.q: What equipment should you buy in months 7â9?
options: B) MIG welder with spool gun
quiz.explanation: A MIG welder with spool gun is suggested for thicker aluminium jobs.

quiz.q: What is the target monthly revenue by months 7â9?
quiz.explanation: Aiming for $3,000â$5,000 monthly revenue is realistic by months 7â9.

quiz.q: What should you do by month 12?
options: B) Have a team of 3â5 people and a certified workshop
quiz.explanation: The goal is to have a team and certification by the end of the year.

quiz.q: Why is a QC logbook important?
options: B) It helps trace problems and improve quality
C) It is required by law
quiz.explanation: A QC logbook allows you to trace issues and maintain consistent quality.

quiz.q: What should you do if a weld fails under warranty?
options: B) Fix it for free and learn why
quiz.explanation: Fixing it for free and learning from the failure protects your reputation.

quiz.q: What is the recommended profit margin for a tender bid?
quiz.explanation: A 20% profit margin is standard for tender bids.
